column3: The name of the decision, describing what algorithm or logic is represented (e.g. pre-eclampsia risk counselling). The decision ID should correspond to the number in the overview table (Table 10).

The description of the decision that needs to be made, based on IF/THEN statements with the appropriate data element name for the variables. The rule should demonstrate the relationship between the input variables and the expected outputs and actions within the decision-support logic – e.g. if blood pressure is higher than 140 systolic/90 diastolic then the client should be flagged as a high-risk pregnancy.
The event that would indicate when this decision-support logic should appear within the workflow, such as the activity that would trigger this decision to be made.

column1: These are the variables or conditions that need to be considered to determine the consequent actions or outputs.
column2: If there are multiple input entries on the same row, these different inputs are considered as “AND” – conditions that need to be in place at the same time.
column3: The resulting action or decision, based on the combination of input entries. This is the statement that immediately follows the “THEN”. Examples of outputs may include a diagnosis or alerts/prompts for referral and/or counselling.
column4: Concrete measures to be taken based on the output (refer, provide treatment and/or counselling, conduct test, etc.). In some cases, output and action may be the same.
column5: Additional explanations or descriptions, including possible pop-up alert messages and relevant background information. This section can also include the written content which would appear in the pop-up messages notifying the health worker of the appropriate next steps, which can include counselling, case management approach, or referral.

column1: Inputs placed on different rows are considered as “OR” conditions that can be considered independently of the inputs on other rows.
